text:
alex: Ran an nsys capture on the perf regression after the kernel-picker changes in PR #4128, attaching highlights below. Timeline looks noisy around warp scheduling and a few kernels dominate now.

kevin: can you paste the top kernels by total GPU time?

alex: sure — extracted from nsys summary (+ perfetto quick view). Top 6 by total time (aggregated across all streams):
```
1) attention_fwd_sm90            38.2%  (replaced earlier attention_fwd_fast)
2) kv_cache_fetch                21.7%
3) softmax_blocked               12.5%
4) kv_scatter_reduce             9.4%
5) layernorm_fwd                 7.1%
6) memcopy_h2d_async             4.8%
other kernels ~6.3%
```

maria: who landed the kernel selector change? I thought we only added a micro-batching heuristic.

lucy: that was me — the heuristic alters kernel choice when seq_len > 1024 and batch interleaving > 4. It favors the sm90 attention path (more numerically stable) but looks like it regresses throughput in our steady-state workload.

sam: timeline screenshots: WARPS stuck in attention_fwd_sm90 with long-active periods, and high L2 request latency spikes coincide with kv_cache_fetch bursts. Attachment: perfetto trace snippet (summary pasted).

kevin: exact counts/metrics from nsys:
```
- attention_fwd_sm90: 880ms total, occupancy 65%, avg SM util 78%
- kv_cache_fetch: 500ms total, occupancy 42%, avg SM util 55%
- softmax_blocked: 290ms, occupancy 58%, avg SM util 61%
- kv_scatter_reduce: 220ms, occupancy 33%, avg SM util 45%
```

alex: two suspects: (1) the sm90 kernel has a higher per-thread register pressure causing lower occupancy; (2) our KV fetch pattern increased memory divergence creating stalls. Both explain the wall-time increase.

lucy: corrected — register pressure is actually similar; the sm90 kernel uses slightly larger shared memory, which pushes block size down on A100/80GB configs, dropping occupancy. The selector didn't account for per-GPU block-size fallback.

maria: repro plan?

alex: steps I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --stats true --trace cuda,cublas python -m scripts/bench_infer --model tiny-rwkv --batch 8 --seq 1536 --streams 6
# perfetto capture for 30s: perfetto --cfg perfetto_cfg.pbtxt -o /tmp/trace.pb
```

sam: quick mitigation candidates: revert selector change, or add a gpu-info table so selector picks kernel variant based on smem availability and compute capability. Also try forcing the old attention_fwd_fast for a canary.

kevin: can you try forcing old kernel with env var and run a smoke nsys to compare? alex?

alex: ran that: forcing attention_fwd_fast drops attention time from 880ms -> 520ms, overall end-to-end down ~28%. KV fetch stays similar, so it's primarily kernel choice.

lucy: OK — I'll add a patch to make kernel choice gating include (smem_per_block, device_cc) and add a small perf test to CI so this doesn't regress silently.

ci-bot: CI perf run scheduled: perf-check/selector-compat on a100-large (will compare attention kernel time vs baseline).

maria: thanks. Let's follow up after the CI perf diff. If that confirms, we'll revert immediate rollout then re-land with the gating. :thumbsup:
